existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Prove an all-n lower bound on the pointwise tensor-independence threshold T(n) of the full n-qubit Gaussian-dyadic Clifford group: its projective tensor Gram is singular at every width f <= 2n, so 2n+1 <= T(n) <= 4n+4 for n >= 2.
scope_change_reason: The formal-interface card is narrowed away from proof-assistant formalization and selected callers to the explicit open question of MatShep PR5675 (does the sharp threshold 4n+1 continue beyond two qubits). This is a written native-interface side result, not a discharge of a selected framework assumption.
bottleneck_link: Side result. Exact native interface tests need widths at or above the Clifford threshold; this proves that any such test window must grow at least like 2n+1 with the qubit count, complementing the 4n+4 sufficient window of PR5526. No kappa or invoice changes.
stop_rule: Ship the first all-n lower bound; do not attempt the three-qubit character computation.
evidence: PROOF.md; verify.py exact finite corroboration (code step for n=2,3,4, cuspidal cosets for n=2,3, literal two-qubit Gram null vectors at widths 1..4, rejection controls)
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact three-qubit threshold T(3), now known to lie in [7,16]?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the 4n+1 pattern of n=1,2 continues, and fixes the sharp native test window at three qubits.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the centre action of the 3-qubit Clifford group (order 4*92,897,280) on class functions at widths 7..13, as #5675 did at two qubits, or find which irreducible characters are absent from the 12th tensor power.
open_questions.blocked_by: No class or character table of the 3-qubit Clifford group is available in the repository; naive enumeration is far beyond the two-qubit method.

open_questions.question: Can Hadamard-type Clifford elements raise the all-n lower bound above 2n+1, toward 4n+1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present residual lives in the Hadamard-free monomial subgroup, whose own threshold is only about 2n+3; the gap to the n=2 value 9 comes from the full group.
open_questions.first_step: At n=2, identify the 1-dimensional determinant-character null vector of #5675 at width 8 and look for an all-n analogue supported on the full group (the determinant itself is trivial for n>=3).
open_questions.blocked_by: No candidate full-group residual is known beyond n=2.
